source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The sR component is a register-value-aware predictor integrated into the Statistical Corrector (SC) of TAGE-SC-L. It captures correlations between branch directions and recently produced register values without explicit dependency tracking. To keep memory port counts feasible, 65 logical registers are partitioned across 8 banks (stride-8: register r belongs to bank r mod 8). For each bank, 3 Usefulness Weight Tables (UT0-UT2, 8 entries each) determine which register currently holding a valid value has the highest correlation usefulness. The 12-bit digest of the selected register is combined with the PC to index 3 Prediction Weight Tables (WT0-WT2: 512, 256, 128 entries of 6-bit weights). The bank's prediction weight sum is conditionally scaled by 2.5 if the register is useful (or gated by 0 if not), and the contributions across all 8 banks are summed to yield the sR correction term.

state.name: reg_status_table
state.organization: Direct-mapped table of 65 logical registers (R0 to R64)
state.entry_format: valid: 1 bit, payload: 14 bits (holds either a 14-bit in-flight ROB tag or a 12-bit register value digest), decay_ctr: 8 bits (saturating instruction counter)
state.indexing: Directly indexed by logical register index (0 to 64)

state.name: usefulness_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Bank 0 tracks 9 registers (R0, R8, ..., R64); Banks 1-7 track 8 registers each
state.entry_format: Bank 0: 9 x 6-bit signed weights (54 bits/entry); Banks 1-7: 8 x 6-bit signed weights (48 bits/entry)
state.indexing: 3-bit folded/skewed index derived from PC: idx = hash(PC) % 8

state.name: prediction_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries)
state.indexing: WT0: 9-bit hash(PC, reg_digest), WT1: 8-bit hash(PC, reg_digest), WT2: 7-bit hash(PC, reg_digest)

algorithms.name: generate_digest
algorithms.trigger: Instruction execution complete / writeback when a 64-bit result value is produced
algorithms.notes: Int count saturation at 63 matches 6-bit width. FP digests are right-aligned to bit 3, leaving bits [2:0] zero. Flag replication fills all 12 bits.

algorithms.name: decode_dispatch_track
algorithms.pseudocode:
for each decoded instruction with destination logical register dest_reg and allocated rob_tag do
  reg_status_table[dest_reg].valid = 0
  reg_status_table[dest_reg].payload = rob_tag & 0x3FFF
  reg_status_table[dest_reg].decay_ctr = 0
end for
// Advance staleness decay for all logical registers
for r = 0 to 64 do
  if reg_status_table[r].valid == 1 then
    if reg_status_table[r].decay_ctr < 255 then
      reg_status_table[r].decay_ctr = reg_status_table[r].decay_ctr + 1
    end if
    if reg_status_table[r].decay_ctr >= 256 then
      reg_status_table[r].valid = 0
    end if
  end if
end for
algorithms.notes: Digests are invalidated after 256 decoded instructions to prevent stale values from polluting predictions.

algorithms.name: execution_complete_update
algorithms.pseudocode:
function on_instruction_complete(dest_reg: int, rob_tag: uint14, result_val: uint64, reg_type: enum):
  if reg_status_table[dest_reg].valid == 0 and reg_status_table[dest_reg].payload == rob_tag then
    reg_status_table[dest_reg].payload = generate_digest(result_val, reg_type)
    reg_status_table[dest_reg].valid = 1
    reg_status_table[dest_reg].decay_ctr = 0
  end if
algorithms.notes: Matches Tomasulo-like tracking: only overwrite payload if the completion corresponds to the latest instruction that claimed dest_reg.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
sR_sum = 0
for bank = 0 to 7 do
  regs_in_bank = list of registers r where (r mod 8 == bank)
  valid_candidates = [r for r in regs_in_bank if reg_status_table[r].valid == 1]
  if valid_candidates is empty then
    bank_contrib[bank] = 0
    continue
  end if

  // Look up 8-entry usefulness tables with skewed PC
  idx0 = hash_ut0(PC, bank) % 8
  idx1 = hash_ut1(PC, bank) % 8
  idx2 = hash_ut2(PC, bank) % 8

  best_reg = -1
  best_usefulness = -INFINITY
  for r in valid_candidates do
    u = usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT0[idx0][r] +
        usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT1[idx1][r] +
        usefulness_weight_tables[bank].UT2[idx2][r]
    if u > best_usefulness then
      best_usefulness = u
      best_reg = r
    end if
  end for

  // Gating condition: scale by 2.5 if useful (> 0), else gate with x0
  if best_usefulness > 0 then
    digest = reg_status_table[best_reg].payload & 0xFFF
    h0 = hash_wt0(PC, digest) % 512
    h1 = hash_wt1(PC, digest) % 256
    h2 = hash_wt2(PC, digest) % 128
    raw_wt_sum = prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT0[h0] +
                 prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT1[h1] +
                 prediction_weight_tables[bank].WT2[h2]
    // Scaled by 2.5 using integer arithmetic: (raw_wt_sum * 5) / 2
    bank_contrib[bank] = (raw_wt_sum * 5) / 2
  else
    bank_contrib[bank] = 0
  end if
  sR_sum = sR_sum + bank_contrib[bank]
end for
return sR_sum
algorithms.notes: sR_sum is forwarded to the SC summing node to compute LSUM = sB + sG + sP + sC + sI + sL + sS + sT + sR. If best_usefulness <= 0 or no registers are valid, bank contribution is 0.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.trigger: Branch commit / retirement when SC update conditions are met
algorithms.pseudocode:
function update_sR(branch_pc: uint64, actual_taken: bool, sc_mispredict: bool, abs_lsum: int, threshold: int):
  if not (sc_mispredict or abs_lsum <= threshold) then
    return
  end if
  for bank = 0 to 7 do
    avail_regs = [r for r in regs_in_bank(bank) if r was valid at prediction time]
    if avail_regs is empty then
      continue
    end if
    // Randomly select one available register to maintain single write port requirement
    r_train = pseudo_random_choice(avail_regs)
    digest = captured_digest_at_pred[r_train]

    // Update prediction weight tables for chosen register
    h0 = hash_wt0(branch_pc, digest) % 512
    h1 = hash_wt1(branch_pc, digest) % 256
    h2 = hash_wt2(branch_pc, digest) % 128
    delta = actual_taken ? +1 : -1
    WT0[h0] = saturate_6bit(WT0[h0] + delta)
    WT1[h1] = saturate_6bit(WT1[h1] + delta)
    WT2[h2] = saturate_6bit(WT2[h2] + delta)

    // Update usefulness table for r_train based on prediction correctness
    idx0 = hash_ut0(branch_pc, bank) % 8
    idx1 = hash_ut1(branch_pc, bank) % 8
    idx2 = hash_ut2(branch_pc, bank) % 8
    pred_agrees = ((WT0[h0] + WT1[h1] + WT2[h2] >= 0) == actual_taken)
    u_delta = pred_agrees ? +1 : -1
    UT0[idx0][r_train] = saturate_6bit(UT0[idx0][r_train] + u_delta)
    UT1[idx1][r_train] = saturate_6bit(UT1[idx1][r_train] + u_delta)
    UT2[idx2][r_train] = saturate_6bit(UT2[idx2][r_train] + u_delta)
  end for
algorithms.notes: Selecting at most one register per bank during update guarantees that each UT and WT bank requires only a single write port.

algorithms.name: pipeline_squash_recovery
algorithms.notes: Completed instructions prior to the squash retain their valid digests, providing immediate value correlation for post-flush restarted instructions.

host_interfaces.need: Destination logical register ID and ROB tag at instruction decode/rename
host_interfaces.description: Used to invalidate the destination register digest and register the in-flight ROB tag in reg_status_table.
host_interfaces.fallback: If decode cannot provide ROB tag, track sequence numbers or physical register IDs.

host_interfaces.need: Result value, destination logical register ID, ROB tag, and operand type at execution completion
host_interfaces.description: Execution units forward completed values to generate 12-bit digests and mark registers valid.
host_interfaces.fallback: If execution forwarding is unavailable, read values from PRF writeback or retirement bus (reduces correlation timeliness).

host_interfaces.description: Increments the 8-bit staleness decay counter across all active registers every decoded instruction.
host_interfaces.fallback: Increment counters per clock cycle or scale decay threshold by average IPC.

host_interfaces.need: Pipeline squash / flush signal with branch ROB tag
host_interfaces.description: Invalidates in-flight pending register tags while preserving digests of completed executions.
host_interfaces.fallback: Flash clear all pending (valid == 0) registers upon branch misprediction recovery.

host_interfaces.description: Accepts sR partial sum to combine into LSUM, and returns SC update triggers during retirement.
host_interfaces.fallback: Implement sR as a standalone perceptron adder stage feeding the final branch chooser.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Prediction Weight Tables (WT): 8 banks x (512 + 256 + 128 entries) x 6 bits = 43,008 bits. Usefulness Weight Tables (UT): 8 banks x 65 registers x (8 + 8 + 8 entries) x 6 bits = 9,360 bits. Register Status Table: 65 registers x (1 valid bit + 14 payload bits + 8 decay_ctr bits) = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.575 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 8 parallel 9-element argmax comparator trees for usefulness selection, 8 fixed-point scaling units ((sum * 5) >> 1), 8-input adder tree for sR, and 12-bit digest generation units in execution units.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: Can shrink TAGE high-bank tagged tables (e.g. reduce 25 banks to 23 banks), decrease Bimodal predictor from 128K entries to 64K entries, or reduce table depths in SC history components (sC, sL, sS, sT).

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales WT entry storage: num_banks * 5,376 bits

parameters.name: num_logical_regs
parameters.storage_impact: Scales UT bits (num_logical_regs * 144 bits) and status table (num_logical_regs * 23 bits)

parameters.name: decay_threshold_insts
parameters.storage_impact: Ceil(log2(decay_threshold_insts)) changes decay_ctr width per register entry

parameters.name: digest_width
parameters.storage_impact: Alters payload width if digest exceeds ROB tag width (14 bits)

parameters.name: wt_weight_width
parameters.storage_impact: Scales WT total storage: 7,168 entries * wt_weight_width

parameters.name: ut_weight_width
parameters.storage_impact: Scales UT total storage: 1,560 entries * ut_weight_width

unit_tests.name: test_int_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: Integer register R1 = 0x000000000000002A (val=42: trailing_zeros=1, leading_zeros=58, LSB6=42)

unit_tests.name: test_fp64_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: FP64 value with sign=1, exponent=0x3FF (top 8 bits of exponent = 0x7F). Val[63:55] = 0x17F (9 bits)

unit_tests.name: test_staleness_invalidation
unit_tests.given: R8 digest marked valid at instruction decode counter T. 256 subsequent instructions decoded without R8 rewrite
unit_tests.expect: At instruction T + 256, reg_status_table[8].valid becomes 0; R8 is ignored in bank 0 usefulness selection

unit_tests.name: test_bank_usefulness_selection
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has valid R0 (UT sum = +5) and valid R8 (UT sum = +12). Skewed PC yields idx0, idx1, idx2
unit_tests.expect: R8 is chosen as best_reg; WT0, WT1, WT2 are indexed using hash(PC, R8.digest)

unit_tests.name: test_multiplier_gating
unit_tests.given: Bank 1 best valid register has net usefulness sum = -2; raw WT sum = +10
unit_tests.expect: Bank 1 contribution is gated to 0 (x0 multiplier applied since usefulness <= 0)

unit_tests.name: test_multiplier_activation
unit_tests.given: Bank 2 best valid register has net usefulness sum = +3; raw WT sum = +8

open_questions: U2: Multiplier wire driving x0 vs x2.5: Assumed to be driven by whether the bank's maximum register usefulness is positive (best_usefulness > 0). Alternative reading: a fixed threshold or a static scale factor without dynamic gating.

U3: Integer leading/trailing bit count encoding: Assumed 6-bit counts saturate at 63, counting leading/trailing identical bits or zeros. Alternative: modulo 64, or counting strictly bits equal to MSB/LSB.

U4: FP register format inspection and alignment: Assumed right-aligned at bit 3 (digest[11:3] for FP64, [8:3] for FP32, [5:3] for FP16, with bits [2:0] = 0). The paper does not specify how hardware classifies unformatted or ambiguous 64-bit values into FP formats.

PRNG policy for single-register update per bank: The paper notes that one available register is randomly selected per bank during update to preserve single write port constraints, but does not specify whether it reuses the 64-bit PRNG seed from Table 2 or an LFSR.

Usefulness weight update threshold: Specific increment/decrement conditions for UT weights are assumed to follow standard TAGE-SC-L usefulness update rules (incremented when sR contribution matches branch outcome).
